spots.name: Château de Caen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Château de Caen is a castle in the Norman city of Caen in the Calvados département (Normandy). It has been officially classed as a Monument historique since 1997.

spots.name: Abbey of Saint-Étienne, Caen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Abbey of Saint-Étienne, also known as Abbaye aux Hommes by contrast with the Abbaye aux Dames, is a former Benedictine monastery in the French city of Caen, Normandy, dedicated to Saint Stephen. It was founded in 1063 by William the Conqueror and is one of the most important Romanesque buildings in Normandy.

spots.name: Abbey of Sainte-Trinité

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Abbey of Sainte-Trinité, better known as the Abbaye aux Dames, is a former Benedictine nunnery in Caen, Normandy. It was the home of the now the Regional Council of Lower Normandy and is now home to the Regional Council of Normandy. The complex includes the Church of Sainte-Trinité.

spots.name: Church of Saint-Pierre

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Saint-Pierre is a Roman Catholic church located on the Place Saint-Pierre in the centre of Caen in Normandy, northern France. It is dedicated to Saint Peter.

spots.name: Mémorial de Caen
spots.summary: The Mémorial de Caen is a museum and war memorial in Caen, Normandy, France commemorating World War II and the Battle for Caen. More generally, the museum is dedicated to the history of the twentieth century, mainly focused on the fragility of peace.

spots.name: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Caen
spots.summary: The Musée des Beaux-Arts de Caen is a fine arts museum in the French city of Caen, founded at the start of the 19th century and rebuilt in 1971 within the ducal château.

spots.name: Church of Saint-Étienne-le-Vieux

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Saint-Étienne-le-Vieux is a former Catholic church, today partly ruined, located in the old city of Caen, Calvados, France. It is not to be confused with the nearby Church of Saint-Étienne, the former church of the Abbaye aux Hommes.

spots.name: Church of Saint-Jean, Caen
spots.summary: The church of Saint-Jean de Caen is the parish church of the Saint-Jean district in Caen, France. It was classified as a historical monument in the list of French historic monuments protected in 1840.

spots.name: Ardenne Abbey

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Abbey of Our Lady of Ardenne, commonly called Ardenne Abbey, is a former Premonstratensian abbey founded in the 12th century and located near Saint-Germain-la-Blanche-Herbe in Calvados, near Caen, France. It is now occupied by the Institute of Contemporary Publishing Archives.

spots.name: Musée de Normandie

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Musée de Normandie is a public museum in Caen, Normandy, France. It has been housed in the Château de Caen since 1963. In June 1970 the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Caen also moved into the castle, expanding the collection.

spots.name: Saint-Sauveur, Caen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Saint-Sauveur is a Roman Catholic church in the historic center of Caen, France. Prior to 1802, it was known as "Notre-Dame-de-Froide-Rue". Since then, the church has been dedicated to the Holy Saviour. The church has been listed as a historical monument since 1889.

spots.name: Église du Vieux Saint-Sauveur

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Old Saint-Sauveur is a former place of worship on the Place Saint-Sauveur in the old town center of Caen, France. Before the French Revolution, the church was a parish and was called just Saint-Sauveur Church.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Caen Synagogue, officially Synagogue of the Hebrew Cultural Association, is a Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 46 Avenue de la Libération, in Caen, Calvados, in the Normandy region of France. The president of the Israelite Cultural Association of Caen (ACI), who own the building, is Nassim Levy.

spots.name: Stade Michel d'Ornano
spots.summary: Stade Michel d'Ornano is a multi-use stadium in Caen, France. It is currently used mostly for football matches and is the home stadium of Stade Malherbe Caen. It is named after the French politician Michel d'Ornano (1924–1991), former president of the Basse-Normandie region.
